items.title: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation
items.summary: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is a promising technology for quantum-secure communications, offering high secret-key rates and straightforward integration with coherent optical communication systems. Conventional Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD encodes information in both optical-field quadratures, increasing requirements for state preparation, modulation, and calibration, while potentially introducing additional preparation imperfections.

items.title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated the ability to generate parameters for variational quantum circuits without conventional optimization. However, the conditions under which this approach is effective remain unclear.

items.title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
items.summary: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation.

items.title: Explicit Absolutely Maximally Entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power
items.summary: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states are pure multipartite states with maximally mixed reductions on every set of at most half the parties. We construct explicit families in local dimension $2q$, twice an odd prime power $q$, using an established coupling of qubits and $q$-level systems.

items.title: Lattice response theory for subsystem symmetry-protected topological phases
items.summary: We develop a framework to study subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases using lattice response theory. We begin with a systematic construction of spacetime lattice gauge fields from general microscopic $X$-type symmetry actions on qudit systems, including global symmetries, subsystem symmetries, and more general modulated symmetries.

items.title: Efficient computation of PEPS gradients for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D topologies
items.summary: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental subroutine for quantum computation. For complex, entangled initial states it is, however, difficult to prepare shallow quantum circuits approximating the state with sufficient accuracy.

items.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
items.summary: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator.

items.title: Gaussian ergotropy and spatial correlations: accelerated vacuum versus a thermal field
items.summary: Can the spatial correlations of a quantum environment be revealed through work extraction? We address this question using two harmonic-oscillator detectors coupled to either an accelerated vacuum or a matched inertial thermal field.

items.title: Noise robust super-Heisenberg scaling in time-dependent quantum sensing by subspace-twirled dynamical decoupling
items.summary: In quantum parameter estimation, time-dependent Hamiltonians can enable ultraprecise estimates of a physical parameter beyond the standard Heisenberg limit, also called the super-Heisenberg limit. However, achieving optimal scaling of the measurement precision typically requires an adaptive quantum control scheme which is resource-intensive and hard to implement in general.

items.title: Physical Observables and Superselection
items.summary: It is well-known that a physical state may be represented by a unit vector in a Hilbert space, whilst a physical observable may be represented by a self-adjoint operator on that same space. However, the introduction of a superselection rule on a Hilbert space imposes constraints such that not all self-adjoint operators can represent observables, which has further consequences for the states themselves as well as the physical processes that transform them.

items.title: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems
items.summary: Certifying entanglement is a central problem in quantum information sciences, especially for continuous-variable quantum systems where full state tomography is experimentally demanding. We introduce a family of separability criteria based on the singular moments and weak moments of the operator obtained by applying the realignment map to the density operator.

items.title: Lorentz Boosts and Governing Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space
items.summary: In solids, the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), $Q_{μν}=g_{μν}-\frac{i}{2} Ω_{μν}$, combines the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Its imaginary part governs anomalous velocity and quantized Hall transport, while its real part determines the quantum weight and geometric contributions to flat-band superfluid stiffness and dielectric response.

items.title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
items.summary: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups.

items.title: Unified master equation for driven multilevel quantum systems: Derivation, dynamics, and spectral signatures
items.summary: Drive-modified dissipation in multilevel quantum systems is not, in general, accurately captured by conventional master equations. We derive a unified master equation using Lewis-Riesenfeld dynamical invariants, accommodating arbitrary driving within Born-Markov theory.

items.title: Communication Supremacy of a Qubit in Holevo Frenkel Weiner Scenario
items.summary: The prevailing wisdom asserts that in the Holevo Frenkel Weiner (HFW) framework of communication tasks, a qubit offers no advantage over a c bit unless additional quantum resources are supplied or the classical shared randomness (SR) is restricted. In contrast, we establish the supremacy of qubit communication in the HFW framework when additional quantum resources, such as entanglement or measurement incompatibility are not injected and SR is a free resource.

items.title: Squeezed terahertz light from nonlinear diamagnetism in ultrastrongly coupled two-dimensional electrons
items.summary: Two-dimensional electron gases in terahertz cavities are among the most mature platforms for ultrastrong light--matter coupling, yet their collective response is captured by the linear Hopfield model, which has an exact classical correspondence. We show that the intrinsic band nonparabolicity of the electrons, recently revealed through nonlinear diamagnetism, turns this system into a quantum Kerr oscillator that squeezes terahertz light.

items.title: When can local unitaries generate a complete orthogonal basis?
items.summary: The question of local encodability asks: can a given, multipartite pure quantum state be completed to an orthonormal basis using only local unitary rotations? If any such state in a given system has this property, it is called universally locally encodable (ULE), a feature, which has applications in quantum information theory, engineering and math.

items.title: Symmetry-Controlled Criticality and Zeno Localization in a Monitored Quasiperiodic Superconductor
items.summary: Measurement-induced transitions of free fermions depend strongly on symmetry, but their interplay with quasiperiodic localization and superconducting pairing remains largely unexplored. We study a continuously monitored model of free fermions with pairing, where quasiperiodicity both controls localization and changes the symmetry class of the monitored field theory.

items.title: Uncertainty-aware quantum machine learning based on Dempster-Shafer theory
items.summary: A large body of work in quantum machine learning has centered on characterizing the expressivity and performance of quantum models. In contrast, little attention has been paid to the reliability of predictions beyond average performance measures such as accuracy.

items.title: The landscape of quantum technology companies in 2026
items.summary: We update our 2022 mapping of 441 quantum technology (QT) companies and examine how the industry has developed. The principal dataset now includes 1,092 companies founded with a QT focus, of which 935 remain active.

items.title: Quantum Keynesian Beauty Contest with Continuous Variables
items.summary: The development of quantum computing has opened up opportunities to re-explore conventional game models by the integration of quantum processes. Through the established framework of quantum game theory, we examine the problem of speculative pricing in the Keynesian Beauty Contest model -- the $p$-Beauty Contest ($p$-BC).

items.title: Finite cyclic monodromy in BMS3 gravity
items.summary: We investigate inducing data for three dimensional asymptotically flat BMS gravity on hyperbolic Virasoro orbits with winding, which contain no constant supermomentum, and the restriction of formal smooth equivariant sections to global Lorentz orbits. Using the developing map of the associated Hill operator we rederive their stabilizer and show that, in the spin double cover, it is the direct product of a line with a cyclic group of even order.

items.title: Non-Convex Optimization via Quantum Tunneling Search on a Photonic Chip
items.summary: Non-convex optimization plays an important role in modern machine learning since plenty of real-world problems have objective functions or constraints with non-convex properties. The non-convex nature of landscapes gives rise to numerous local minima and saddle points, dramatically hindering the ability of gradient descent-based methods to explore the landscape and obtain global optima.

items.title: Key Relay and Secure Network Coding: One-Shot Equivalence and Separation on Undirected Networks
items.summary: Motivated by quantum key distribution networks, we compare key relay protocols with secure network coding on the same undirected graph. In this comparison, we fix the finite field, terminal set, and wiretap family.

items.title: Inter-city 18.9 km free-space QKD over a dense urban corridor
items.summary: Terrestrial free-space quantum key distribution (QKD) provides a flexible complement to fiber-based networks, but its deployment over long horizontal paths in dense metropolitan environments remains challenging, as atmospheric turbulence, demanding pointing and tracking requirements, and operational constraints can substantially increase system complexity. We experimentally demonstrate the operation of a decoy-state BB84 system over an 18.9~km free-space link across a densely populated urban area in the…

items.title: Reduced filtering using classical control hierarchy with linear optimality for continuous quantum error correction
items.summary: Continuous quantum error correction promises reduced thresholds and hardware overhead compared to the digital paradigm, but its complex model estimation has greatly reduced its practicality. We recast this problem as a classical control-theoretic state hierarchy made of an exact bilinear reduced model, an exact conditional filter, and standard estimation and feedback design.

items.title: Detecting non-Hermitian topology from long-time dynamics
items.summary: We propose a protocol to measure the non-Hermitian topological invariant associated with the Lindbladian spectrum of chiral-symmetric open Gaussian systems from the relaxation of the covariance matrix. Importantly, the method works in the long-time regime and does not rely on isolating edge modes, so it remains applicable even when the Liouvillian skin effect may obscure them.

items.title: Ground-State Spin Squeezing and Collective Excitations in $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Symmetric Systems
items.summary: Ground-state spin squeezing is a resource for quantum-enhanced measurements, but is commonly associated with a closing excitation gap near a quantum critical point. A closing gap can complicate state preparation and reduce thermal robustness.

items.title: Probabilistic distillation of superposition
items.summary: How well a superposition of nonorthogonal states, such as an optical cat state, serves as a resource depends on how its components interfere. Here we determine the optimal probability of converting one such superposition into another by superposition-free operations.

items.title: Reply to the Comment by Hradil and Řeháček
items.summary: Hradil and Řeháček argue that the quantum metrological advantage demonstrated in our squeezed-vacuum phase-sensing experiment disappears, when measurement repetitions and total photon resources are properly accounted for. We show that this conclusion is mathematically unfounded and that neither resource accounting nor finite-sample statistical considerations invalidate the demonstrated quantum-enhanced local phase sensitivity.

items.title: Residual Entanglement vs. Residual Coherence: A Wave Packet Approach in Neutrino Oscillation with Matter
items.summary: In this work, we investigate quantum correlations in three-flavor neutrino oscillations beyond the standard plane-wave (PW) description by employing a wave-packet formalism in the presence of constant matter density. We study three quantum correlation measures, namely the residual $l_1$-norm coherence, Concurrence Fill, and Three-$π$ entanglement, and express them in terms of transition probabilities for an initial muon-flavor state.

items.title: Thermodynamically Consistent Quantum-Classical Hybrid Dynamics: A Metriplectic Approach to Generalized Lindblad and Bloch-Torrey Equations
items.summary: We develop a metriplectic framework for quantum--classical hybrid dynamics that ensures thermodynamic consistency through conservation of energy and non-negative entropy production. The approach combines a hybrid Poisson bracket with a metriplectic $4$-bracket, with coupling between quantum and classical subsystems arising solely through dissipative processes.

items.title: Persistent-mediator architecture for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation with color codes
items.summary: Two-dimensional color codes provide transversal Clifford gates, whereas suitable three-dimensional codes provide a transversal $T$ gate. Representative cross-dimensional schemes either switch the computational encoding or consume a 3D encoded state.

items.title: Hilbert's 17th problem for symmetric functions: undecidability and a counterexample
items.summary: We study inequalities between symmetric functions that hold in every number of variables. First, we prove that it is undecidable whether a symmetric function with rational coefficients is nonnegative in all dimensions, answering a question posed by Acevedo, Blekherman, Debus and Riener.

items.title: Geometric Theory of Quasiperiodically Driven Systems
items.summary: Quasiperiodically driven systems give rise to a rich set of physical phenomena in contemporary quantum physics, with applications ranging from nonequilibrium dynamics to Hamiltonian engineering and control. However, unlike periodically driven (Floquet) systems, their study is hindered by the absence of a generic theory to describe their evolution using an effective time-independent Hamiltonian and its eigenstates.

items.title: Automatic O(a) Improvement for Wilson Twisted Mass Fermions in the Hamiltonian Formulation
items.summary: We apply the recently developed Symanzik effective Hamiltonian framework to Wilson twisted mass fermions. The effective Hamiltonian is constructed solely based on the symmetries of the lattice Hamiltonian without recourse to the Symanzik effective action in Euclidean space-time.

items.title: Quantum tunneling of a measurement-driven active particle
items.summary: Active particles can exhibit persistent motion set by their orientation. We demonstrate this key property for a quantum active particle: The particle's motion is locked to the orientation of its spin due to spin-orbit coupling and damping, and the orientation is made persistent through continuous measurement via the quantum Zeno effect.

items.title: A Quantum Algorithm for Computing All Eigenvalues and Eigenstates of Sparse Hermitian Matrices
items.summary: Computation of eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a sparse Hermitian matrix is a fundamental problem in algebra, arising both as a problem of independent interest and as a key subroutine in a wide range of computational and scientific applications. In this work, we develop a quantum algorithm that determines the spectrum of a sparse Hermitian matrix, defined as the set of its distinct eigenvalues, and for each eigenvalue, prepares a corresponding eigenvector as a quantum state in its eigenspace.

items.title: Beauty and charm jet identification with end-to-end training on a superconducting quantum processor
items.summary: The identification of heavy-flavor jets, i.e. collimated streams of particles originating from the fragmentation of beauty and charm quarks produced in proton-proton collisions, represents one of the most challenging classification tasks in measurements at Large Hadron Collider experiments.

items.title: Gatemon qubits based on in-situ ternary InAsSb/Al nanowire Josephson junctions
items.summary: Ternary InAsSb/Al nanowires combine compositionally engineerable semiconductor properties with epitaxial proximity superconductivity, making them attractive for hybrid quantum circuits and mesoscopic superconductivity. Here, we realize gatemon qubits based on shadow-defined in-situ InAsSb/Al Josephson junctions in a single growth process.

items.title: Noise-Protected Superconducting Qudits from Higher-Harmonic Josephson Junctions
items.summary: Qudits, which generalize qubits to $d$ levels, store more information per circuit element than qubits. As with qubits, however, their sensitivity to noise must be overcome before they can be used for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

items.title: Effect of atomic interactions on quantum communication protocols
items.summary: We develop a first-principles framework for analyzing photonic quantum communication in an atomic medium. Starting from a real-space quantization of the electromagnetic field coupled to an ensemble of two-level atoms, we derive an effective model for polarization-encoded single-photon states.

items.title: Quantum Mpemba effect from logical-information exposure in monitored circuits
items.summary: In the Mpemba effect, a state initially farther from stationarity overtakes one that starts closer. After one cycle in a monitored Clifford chain, an unencoded Bell-pair state has lower mean entanglement entropy than a scrambled reference prepared from fewer pairs.

items.title: Symmetry and quasi-gauge invariance of Krylov complexity
items.summary: Krylov spread complexity quantifies how extensively a quantum system explores its Hilbert space during time evolution. We identify two classes of unitary transformations that preserve the complexity of the associated dynamics, and relate this property to the invariance of the energy distribution of the initial state and of its associated Hamiltonian moments.

items.title: Learning Sparse Graph States with Local Pauli Measurements: Tight Nonadaptive Bounds and an Adaptive Separation
items.summary: We study how many copies of an unknown $n$-qubit graph state are needed to identify its graph when every qubit is measured in the $X$, $Y$ or $Z$ basis. Ouyang and Tomamichel showed that $O(d^2\log n)$ copies suffice for $d$-regular graphs, while any measurement needs $Ω(d\log n)$, and asked whether the quadratic dependence on $d$ is necessary.

items.title: Circuit-Level Analysis of Quantum Error Correction in Second-Generation Quantum Repeaters
items.summary: We present a circuit-level simulation of second-generation quantum repeaters with stabilizer-based quantum error correction. We model a two-segment repeater link including encoding, syndrome extraction, decoding, and entanglement swapping, and compare the performance of the single-error-correcting Steane and five-qubit stabilizer codes under different noise scenarios.

items.title: Engineering Bosonic Steady States through Fock-Space Currents
items.summary: Fock states are valuable resources for quantum technologies, but intrinsic loss makes their stabilization challenging. Whereas existing stabilization schemes are typically formulated for specific microscopic processes, here we develop a unified Fock-space current-engineering framework for the autonomous stabilization of selectable Fock states.

items.title: Exact Quantum Algorithms for Composed Boolean Functions
items.summary: We study exact quantum algorithms for block compositions of total Boolean functions. For an outer function $f$ of degree $D$ and an inner function $g$ on $m$ bits, we prove $$ Q_E(f\circ g)=O\!\left(mD+Q_E(f)Q_{1/(4D)}(g)\right).

items.title: Probing the extreme quantum violation of the Leggett-Garg inequality
items.summary: The Leggett-Garg (LG) inequalities were formulated for testing the incompatibility between the classical worldview of macrorealism and quantum theory. By analogy with the Tsirelson bound for Bell inequalities, the maximal quantum violation of LG inequalities is commonly referred to as the temporal Tsirelson bound (TTB).

items.title: Loss of the quadratic speedup in Grover search under local and coherent noise
items.summary: Grover's algorithm searches an unstructured database with a number of oracle queries that grows only as the square root of its size. Noise erodes this advantage, and we ask, analytically, how quickly.

items.title: No Convergence in Learned Eavesdropping-Detection Dynamics for BB84 Quantum Key Distribution
items.summary: In prior work we showed that a reinforcement-learning eavesdropper can intercept BB84 quantum key distribution while holding the quantum bit error rate below the abort threshold and keeping a usable distillable key. In this paper we ask whether an equally adaptive learning detector can close this stealth window.

items.title: Generation and conversion of vortex light in coherently prepared hydrogen atoms and hydrogen-like ions
items.summary: We propose a theoretical scheme for generating and converting optical vortices in a coherently prepared three-level Λ-type atomic medium. An azimuthally varying relative phase between the two lower states imparts additional phase winding to the generated field, yielding l2=l1+m in the ideal model, where l1 is the input topological charge and m the coherence winding number.

items.title: An optical-frequency-comb-enabled unified infrastructure for quantum networks
items.summary: Quantum networks require precision timing and classical communication to coordinate distributed quantum operations, yet these functions are typically supported by separate infrastructures, increasing system complexity and limiting scalability. Here we demonstrate an optical-frequency-comb-enabled infrastructure that unifies precision timing, classical communication and quantum communication over a shared fibre link.

items.title: Collective information backflow from a local population record: Identifiability and learning
items.summary: Information backflow in a composite quantum system is defined through pairs of evolving states, whereas an experiment may provide only a restricted population record. We study this mismatch for two identical qubits coupled collectively to a vacuum reservoir with an exponential correlation function.

items.title: Information Thermodynamics in Closed Quantum Many-Body Dynamics
items.summary: Although information thermodynamics explains how the second law is modified due to the information acquired by Maxwell's demon, its formulation in many-body systems remains largely open. Here, we develop an information-thermodynamic framework for closed quantum many-body systems initially in microscopic thermal equilibrium (MITE), under physically motivated restrictions: local quantum measurements and finite-time controls generated by local Hamiltonians.

items.title: Optically-detected room-temperature spin-coherence from the GaV$^-$ in diamond
items.summary: Solid-state quantum defects (point crystal imperfections with optically addressable spins) are among the most promising platforms for quantum information science due to their long-lived electron and nuclear spin lifetimes. The negatively-charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) and negatively-charged group IV vacancies (G4V's) in diamond are some the most promising quantum defects but, the NV$^-$ is highly susceptible to charge noise and has low emission from its zero-phonon line while the G4V's require low operating…

items.title: Hierarchical Decoding for Quantum Error Correction
items.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires classical decoders that can keep up with syndrome data streams and supply correction information and logical measurement outcomes to the quantum control system. Meeting these requirements at scale requires high throughput while controlling the end-to-end latency from readout to usable correction.

items.title: Anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior driven by dichotomous Markov noise in a quantum Ising chain: Generalized stochastic resonance in the defect density
items.summary: The anti-Kibble-Zurek behavior may arise under noise, adding a noise-induced contribution to the defect density beyond the conventional Kibble-Zurek term. Most investigations of such behavior have so far been restricted to Gaussian noise.

items.title: Probing chaos and criticality with observational entropy and finite-resolution measurements
items.summary: Coarse-grained measurements offer a scalable alternative to full state tomography for characterizing complex quantum dynamics. We show that observational entropy (OE), an information-theoretic entropy defined directly from finite-resolution measurement outcomes, provides a unified and experimentally accessible framework for quantifying chaos and probing criticality.

items.title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
items.summary: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. Its purpose is to demonstrate why colleges must prepare now, well before fault tolerant quantum computers arrive, by developing quantum ready capacities across curriculum, workforce development, partnerships and cybersecurity.

items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms: A Comprehensive Guide
items.summary: This book offers a rigorous and forward-looking exploration of one of the most consequential frontiers in modern computation: the use of quantum mechanics to accelerate search, optimization, learning, simulation, and secure information processing. It begins by establishing the conceptual and mathematical foundations of quantum computation, including quantum gates, circuit design, quantum parallelism, and the distinctions between classical and quantum models of information processing.

items.title: Attention Renders Sensory Contents into Conscious State via Content-invariant Frontal-Posterior Coupling in Humans
items.summary: Abstract Although attention promotes conscious perception, how it does so remains unclear. Human neuroimaging research has richly characterized attentional modulation upon visual processing, yet it remains unclear which of its components act as precursors of consciousness, which constitute consciousness itself, and which merely reflect post-perceptual, response-related operations.

items.title: OUCH: Objective, Uniform, Controlled Haptic Stimulation for Automated Neurological Assessment
items.summary: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. In standard bedside assessments, these stimuli are applied manually, resulting in substantial variation in force, duration, frequency, and location.

items.title: Digital Minds: Issues in the Philosophy of Mind and Cognitive Science
items.summary: ABSTRACT This article provides a contemporary introduction to issues in the philosophy of mind and cognitive science that are studied within the emerging field of digital minds research. We explore the potential for AI systems to have mental states.

items.title: The Sociological Cogito and the Hard Problems of Science: Math, Logic, God, and Consciousness as Social Phenomena
items.summary: This groundbreaking work introduces the sociological cogito as a revolutionary paradigm for solving the most perplexing “hard problems” in science and philosophy: mathematics, logic, God, and consciousness. By challenging traditional Cartesian and Platonist approaches, it demonstrates how these seemingly transcendental phenomena are actually grounded in our social realities.

items.title: Illusionism as a theory of mental content
items.summary: Analytic philosophers of mind seemingly take the hard problem of consciousness to be the only aspect of the mind-body problem that has not been in principle solved. But phenomenal consciousness is not the only puzzling and mysterious mental phenomena.

items.title: Everettian chance in no uncertain terms
items.summary: Abstract The current landscape of views on the role of chance in the Everett interpretation is rocky. Everettians (Wallace, 2012; Sebens and Carroll, 2018; McQueen and Vaidman, 2019) agree that chance values should be derived using rules of rationality governing agents’ uncertain reasoning and/or decision-making, but they cannot agree on how.
items.source: European Journal for Philosophy of Science

items.title: Unitarity with respect to the clock of a dynamical local observer and the Einstein equivalence principle
items.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution relative to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity.

items.title: Pharmacokinetics of Local Anesthetics in Fascial Plane Blocks: Clinical Implications and Safety Considerations-A Narrative Review
items.summary: Fascial plane blocks (FPBs) are increasingly used in modern regional anaesthesia and differ from conventional nerve blocks by delivering local anesthetic (LA) into interfascial compartments. This approach results in distinct pharmacokinetics with clinically relevant systemic absorption.

items.summary: This book offers a multidisciplinary and business-focused exploration of AI and computing, highlighting their potential impact on digital commerce, entrepreneurship,and innovation. It critically examines the shift towards data-driven technologies as organisations strive to enhance value creation, operational efficiency, and customer experience.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle--hole-invariant momenta fix the bulk $\mathbb Z_2$ invariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: Quantum Forensics in Cybercrime Investigation and Digital Forensics: From Digital Footprints to Strategic Decision-Making
items.summary: This paper proposes Quantum Forensics as a novel theoretical and applied paradigm for cybercrime investigation and digital forensics. The central thesis is that proving evidence in cyber crimes demands a dual approach: a quantitative, reproducible STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) method that demonstrates evidence significance scientifically, and an inferential method that connects facts to law through evidentiary frameworks spanning national legislation, international conventions, UNCITRAL…

items.title: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis
items.summary: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis Abstract (EN) The hard problem of consciousness asks why physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience. This paper offers a reformulation of the problem within the Acta Universi (AU) hypothesis—a speculative informational-entropic ontology.

items.title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
items.summary: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia.

items.title: From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
items.summary: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability.

items.title: Patient-specific factors are associated with distinct brain network connectivity in disorders of consciousness
items.summary: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) arise from diverse etiologies and exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity, including variations in patient age and time since injury. However, how these clinical characteristics relate to large-scale brain network connectivity and are associated with consciousness levels and functional outcomes remains poorly understood.

items.title: Spin-Based Quantum Information Processing in Cytoskeletal Filaments Using Nucleoside Phosphates
items.summary: Abstract Phosphorus nuclear spins are candidates for quantum information processing in biological matter because 31P is a spin-1/2nucleus without an electric quadrupole moment, although coherence remains environment-dependent. Recent work rangesfrom theoretical proposals based on phosphate ions and Posner molecules to experimental demonstrations of room-temperaturequantum logic in adenosine diphosphate.

items.title: Safety-First, Severity-Adapted Enhanced Recovery After Surgery for Patients with Neurodegenerative Disorders: A Narrative Review and Proposed Framework
items.summary: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways have been shown to improve perioperative outcomes in broad surgical populations. However, their safety, feasibility, and optimal adaptation remain uncertain in patients with neurodegenerative disorders (NDDs), particularly those with dementia and Parkinson's disease.

items.title: Distinguishing gagging, nausea, retching, and vomiting: A multidimensional psychophysiological framework
items.summary: Gagging, nausea, retching, and vomiting are often reported together clinically, but differ in their triggers, subjective features, motor organization, and relation to expulsion. This narrative review compares them using human studies, research on airway protection, and animal models of emesis.

items.title: Operationally induced preferred basis in unitary quantum mechanics
items.summary: Abstract The preferred-basis problem remains under unitary system–apparatus dynamics, whereas measurements have mutually exclusive outcomes. The present framework places basis selection in the complete preparation–measurement arrangement.

items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Anesthesia via Dissociative Overload: A Unified Theoretical Framework Linking DMT and Ketamine Through Sigma-1 Convergence, Entropic Saturation, and Workspace Flooding
items.summary: General anesthesia has long been understood as a unitary phenomenon driven by neural suppression — a reduction in cortical activity, entropy, and complexity that renders the brain unable to sustain conscious processing. Yet two structurally and pharmacologically distinct compounds, N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) and ketamine, produce clinical unresponsiveness while maintaining or increasing cortical complexity, a pattern fundamentally incompatible with the suppression paradigm.

items.title: Nonlocality as a benchmarking tool for quantum processors
items.summary: Abstract Benchmarking quantum processors is a central task in every roadmap aimed at quantum advantage. Here, we discuss a benchmarking protocol based on the violation of the Svetlichny inequality, which is designed to simulate genuine multipartite nonlocality.

items.title: Qualia Is Not a Pseudoproblem: A Response to Balconi et al. (2026), 'The End of Qualia'
items.summary: A response to Balconi et al.'s (2026) Frontiers in Psychology editorial proposing that qualia be retired as a pseudoproblem in Kuhn's sense. The letter argues that the collection the editorial introduces does not support its eliminative frame; that a malformed question has never licensed abandoning the phenomenon it names; and that first-person report remains the foundation on which pain science, affective neuroscience, and clinical measurement were built — the reports came first, and the instruments followed them.

items.title: Where Intention Goes, Responsibility Flows: Grounding AI Accountability in the Machine Learning Paradigm
items.summary: An opening salvo of lawsuits in U.S. courts has begun holding AI companies accountable through independent doctrinal routes: product liability and agency law cut as swords, while the shields of Section 230 immunity and First Amendment doctrine begin to crack.

items.title: Adaptive sensing beyond non-adaptive information limits: End-to-end co-design of geometry, policy, and inference
items.summary: Inverse design has transformed vast physical parameter spaces into a substrate for emergent functionality, raising the tantalizing prospect of relocating intelligence from the digital domain into the physical world itself. Nowhere is this prospect more consequential than in sensing, where the analog-to-digital interface imposes a fundamental bottleneck: information not captured by the hardware is irrevocably lost to any downstream algorithm.

items.title: Preserved consciousness as a diagnostic pitfall: a probable case of tramadol-induced serotonergic toxicity with isolated neuromuscular symptoms in an adolescent after general anesthesia
items.summary: Serotonin syndrome (SS) typically presents with altered mental status, autonomic dysfunction, and neuromuscular abnormalities. We report an atypical case of perioperative tramadol-induced serotonergic toxicity in an adolescent characterized by isolated neuromuscular symptoms with completely preserved consciousness and stable autonomic function, challenging the established paradigm that altered mental status and hyperthermia are obligatory for diagnosis.

items.title: Quantum radar: An engineering perspective
items.summary: Quantum radar has emerged as a promising sensing paradigm that exploits quantum resources, including entanglement and quantum correlations, to enhance target detection in noisy and lossy environments. Although entanglement generated by superconducting devices such as Josephson parametric amplifiers, Josephson parametric converters, and Josephson traveling-wave parametric amplifiers is rapidly degraded under realistic propagation conditions, the remaining quantum correlations can still provide a measurable…

items.title: Generative graph neural networks for inverse design of cQED circuits
items.summary: Superconducting quantum circuits are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing, but their design remains a complex inverse problem, requiring the identification of circuit architectures and physical parameters capable of reproducing a desired quantum response. Existing approaches mainly rely on iterative optimization, predefined topologies, or previously simulated device families, limiting their flexibility as circuit complexity increases.

items.title: Human consciousness versus the scientific method
items.summary: This study explores how science has approached the complex phenomenon of human consciousness, emphasizing the challenges of addressing subjectivity through objective and replicable methodologies. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database, identifying 1,143 documents between 1990 and 2024.
items.source: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews

items.title: Minimal and Moderate Sedation Agents
items.summary: Sedation refers to a medically induced alteration in consciousness intended to reduce anxiety, promote relaxation, and facilitate patient cooperation. This chapter focuses on the pharmacologic agents most commonly used in minimal and moderate pediatric dental sedation.

items.title: Arrival-time problem in the quantum information era - observation of a Zeno crossover in monitored arrival-time distributions
items.summary: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits.

items.title: An Empirical Study on Clustering-based Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm for Regression Test Case Selection
items.summary: Regression testing assesses whether software components that have already been developed and tested continue to work correctly after modifications. Ideally, regression testing re-executes the entire test suite after each modification, but this is infeasible in real-world scenarios because of the computational burden; therefore, optimized approaches, such as Test Case Selection, have been developed.

items.title: Adaptive Protocol for Rényi Entropy Estimation
items.summary: The second-order Rényi entropy is one of the most important quantities used for characterizing the entanglement structure of states prepared in quantum many-body experiments. With access to qubit projective measurement data, it can be estimated via a protocol in which repeated measurements are taken after each of a set of random local unitary operations is applied to the quantum state.

items.title: Dynamical Light-Matter Coupling with Protected Superconducting Oscillators
items.summary: Superconducting circuits hosting long-lived bosonic modes are an excellent platform for emulating the dynamics of light and matter and exploiting them for quantum information processing. The space of accessible dynamics is greatly extended by introducing the frequency tunability of artificial atoms, whereby the interactions with the light field of a microwave cavity can be modified on demand.

items.title: Quantum Open Effective Field Theory: anomalous decoherence
items.summary: We study decoherence of a scalar field coupled to ``anomalous'' environments with critical behavior with the Schwinger-Keldysh including the influence functional, and the quantum master equation (QME) up to second order in the coupling. The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation yields a Langevin equation and the Lindblad (QME) includes \emph{time dependent rates} allowing to study transient dynamics.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We propose an extension to Schrödinger’s equation that incorporates macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse. We find that a hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in accordance with Born’s rule.

items.title: A Quantum-Classical Surrogate Model for the Collision Operator of the Lattice Boltzmann Method
items.summary: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers.

items.title: Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Advances
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative condition accompanied by widespread central nervous system damage and complex networked pathogenesis spanning molecular, cellular, and systemic dimensions.
